Theta GmbH’s strategy of filing for multiple patents on next-generation wireless communication represents a classic defensive and offensive intellectual property maneuver. By securing a temporary monopoly, they are effectively raising the barrier to entry for competitors, including our business. This move is likely to impede our development efforts by forcing us to navigate around their patented technologies or risk litigation, which can be costly and time-consuming. Consequently, we may be compelled to seek alternative solutions, potentially leading to increased R&D costs, delayed product launches, or the adoption of less optimal technical paths. This could erode our competitive advantage and market share if we fail to innovate around their patents quickly and efficiently.

A book is primarily made of paper.
